reason: E1 directly supports the existence of mesoscopic domains and the role of Cr and Mn in their formation, but it provides no evidence that these domains act as dislocation obstacles or that their removal alters mechanical properties as predicted.
premises: Mesoscopic chemically modulated domains exist in single-phase FCC CrMnFeCoNi.
These domains are promoted by Cr and Mn interactions.
These domains act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
Domain presence/evolution modifies work hardening and failure behavior.
Removing Cr or Mn reduces domain formation and degrades mechanical properties.
